transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, the main thing is I’m having a really hard time with tasks that take sustained mental effort. Like at work, if I have to sit down and do monthly reports or plan something bigger, like a multi-site health event, it’s like I hit a wall. I keep putting it off even though I know it’s important, and it’s starting to be a real problem.
Do you find yourself feeling excessively worried or anxious about things, even when there isn’t a clear reason for concern?
Not really, no. I mean, I worry about things when there’s something actually going on, like a deadline or problem at work, but I wouldn’t say I’m anxious for no clear reason.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or have you lost interest in activities that you usually enjoy, even when there isn’t a specific work-related stressor going on?

I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed feeling depressed or losing interest in things in general. It’s more that I get frustrated when work stuff piles up, but outside of that, I wouldn’t say I’m down for no reason.
Do you have similar difficulties with tasks or staying organized in other areas of your life, like managing personal errands, household chores, or even following through on plans with friends?

Yeah, it does happen outside of just the main work tasks. When I’m juggling work projects, memorial committee stuff, and outreach events, I’ll have notes in three different places, and then I can’t seem to sort out what needs to happen first. I end up leaving things too late and rushing at the end.
Have you had similar issues with staying organized, keeping track of tasks, or misplacing things for most of your life, even going back to when you were in school?

Yeah, it goes back pretty far. Even in elementary school, teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but I was always daydreaming or losing worksheets. I’d forget to turn in homework unless my mom checked my backpack every night.
Do you also struggle with staying focused or organized in settings that aren’t work-related, like at home, while driving, or during conversations with friends?

Yes, I do. Even in meetings, I’ll be trying to follow something like a budget update, and then a phone buzzing, people talking out in the hall, or even just a random thought about something I forgot for the league will pull me away. Then I realize I missed the next few minutes of what was being said.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble staying seated, especially in situations where you're expected to remain still or quiet?
Not really, no. I mean, I might shift in my chair sometimes like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’m especially restless or that I can’t stay seated when I’m supposed to.
Do these issues with focus and organization cause you problems in your social life, at work, or in other important areas of your life?

Yes, it does. I mean, I’m still functioning — I get by at work and in the community — but it causes problems. People have had to cover for things I missed or forgot, and some deadlines have slipped because I didn’t stay on top of them.

Socially too, I’ve had to make last-minute apologies to coworkers or friends when I dropped the ball, and that’s embarrassing. It’s not like everything is falling apart, but it definitely affects me.
Do you notice these issues with focus and getting things done in different places — like at home, in social situations, and at work — or do they only happen in one specific setting?

It happens in more than one setting. I notice it at work, but also with people outside work. I’m still getting by, but there are gaps — people have had to cover for me when I missed something, deadlines have slipped, and I’ve had to make last-minute apologies to coworkers or friends. It’s embarrassing, honestly.
Do you often find yourself getting distracted by things around you, like sounds or sights, or even your own thoughts, even when you’re trying to focus on something important?

Yes, that happens pretty often. Like in meetings, I’ll be trying to listen to a budget update, and then a phone vibrates or I hear people talking out in the hall, and I’m just gone for a minute. Sometimes it’s not even something outside — I’ll suddenly think about something I forgot to do for the league, and then I realize I missed the next few minutes of what was being said.
